# ledger_merchant_alias (Resource)

A name that Ledger matches transactions to a merchant by. A name belongs to one merchant at most (compared ignoring case and white space), so adding one that another merchant has fails with `merchant_alias_taken`. If the merchant already has the name (every merchant has its display name), this resource takes it over, and destroying the resource removes that alias. An alias cannot be changed: a new name replaces the resource. Merchant routes need an API token with the administrator-only `merchants:read` and `merchants:write` grants (merchant names derive from bank text).

Import with `<merchant_id>/<alias_id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A name Ledger matches transactions to the merchant by. A name belongs to one merchant at most.
resource "ledger_merchant_alias" "grocer_branch" {
  merchant_id = ledger_merchant.grocer.id
  name        = "LIDL VILNIUS"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `merchant_id` (String) The identifier of the merchant. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `name` (String) The alias name, 1 to 200 characters, as Ledger stores it (trimmed, white space collapsed). Changing it replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `alias_id` (String) The alias identifier.
- `id` (String) `<merchant_id>/<alias_id>`.
- `key` (String) The name as matched: Unicode NFC, white space collapsed, lower case.
- `origin` (String) How the alias came to be: `user` (the API), `decision` (a confirmation or correction named it) or `upgrade`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <merchant_id>/<alias_id>
terraform import ledger_merchant_alias.grocer_branch 01JD3Y4C8V9M2Q7W5R6T0XZBNA/01JD3Y4C8V9M2Q7W5R6T0XZBNB
```
